title: The PAR-score based on PANoptosis genes predicts the progression of ulcerative colitis and the response to anti-TNF-alpha treatment.
authors: Li, Yantong; Yin, Xisheng; Zheng, Shi; Zhao, Yong; Zhong, Xiaolin
one_liner_zh: 该文基于PANoptosis基因构建溃疡性结肠炎风险评分，聚焦炎症疾病预测与药物筛选，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ulcerative colitis (UC), a chronic inflammatory bowel disease, carries an elevated risk of colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC). While PANoptosis-a coordinated cell death mechanism integrating pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis-has been linked to inflammatory disorders, its role in UC progression and CAC transformation remains undefined. OBJECTIVE: To delineate PANoptosis-related signatures and develop predictive models for the assessment of UC and CAC. METHODS: Transcriptomic data from UC patients, CAC cases, and controls (GEO database) were analyzed to identify PANoptosis-associated genes. Enrichment and immune infiltration analyses elucidated functional roles, while a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine colitis model validated candidate gene expression via Western blot. Single-cell sequencing dissected cellular heterogeneity, Mendelian randomization established causality, and molecular docking screened therapeutic agents. RESULTS: Four PANoptosis hub genes (CASP1, LCN2, STAT3, ZBP1) were identified as UC drivers. The PANoptosis-Associated Risk Score (PAR-Score) demonstrated robust diagnostic accuracy (AUC > 0.75) and stratified disease activity, anti-TNF-alpha responsiveness, and CAC risk. Molecular docking revealed strong binding affinity between epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitors and target proteins (binding energy: -6.0 to -8.4 kcal/mol), suggesting therapeutic potential. CONCLUSION: The PAR-Score based on PANoptosis genes predicts the progression of UC and the response to anti-TNF-alpha treatment. EGFR inhibitors may serve as potential therapeutic agents for UC and CAC.
abstract_zh: 背景：溃疡性结肠炎（ulcerative colitis, UC）是一种慢性炎症性肠病，其结肠炎相关结直肠癌（colitis-associated colorectal cancer, CAC）风险升高。尽管PANoptosis——一种整合焦亡、凋亡和坏死性凋亡的协调性细胞死亡机制——已被关联至炎症性疾病，但其在UC进展及CAC转化中的作用仍不明确。目的：描绘PANoptosis相关特征，并开发用于评估UC和CAC的预测模型。方法：分析来自UC患者、CAC病例及对照组（GEO数据库）的转录组数据，以识别PANoptosis相关基因。富集和免疫浸润分析阐明了功能角色，而葡聚糖硫酸钠（dextran sulfate sodium, DSS）诱导的小鼠结肠炎模型通过Western blot验证了候选基因表达。单细胞测序解析了细胞异质性，孟德尔随机化确立了因果关系，分子对接筛选了治疗药物。结果：四个PANoptosis枢纽基因（CASP1、LCN2、STAT3、ZBP1）被确定为UC驱动因子。PANoptosis相关风险评分（PAR-Score）显示出稳健的诊断准确性（AUC > 0.75），并对疾病活动度、抗TNF-α应答及CAC风险进行了分层。分子对接揭示了表皮生长因子受体（epidermal growth factor receptor, EGFR）抑制剂与靶蛋白之间的强结合亲和力（结合能：-6.0至-8.4 kcal/mol），提示其治疗潜力。结论：基于PANoptosis基因的PAR-Score可预测UC进展及对抗TNF-α治疗的应答。EGFR抑制剂可能作为UC和CAC的潜在治疗药物。
